Hi Grace — thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines our procurement team asked me to share so we can move this forward internally. High level items: 1) they want the minimum committed spend reduced from $200,000 to $150,000, with the option to make up the difference in Q2 if needed; 2) invoicing cadence should be monthly in arrears rather than quarterly; 3) they require Net 45 payment terms (our AP process is Net 45) and a Purchase Order on every invoice; 4) VAT handling — they asked Redwood to confirm whether Redwood will invoice gross (we're VAT registered in a few EU countries) or whether they should self-assess (reverse charge).

Can you confirm what flexibility you have on minimums and the practical implications of switching to monthly invoices + Net 45? Also attaching the PO template they insisted we include. We have a launch target of Jan 2027 so timeline is a bit tight.

Kimberly / Grace — forwarding Evan's redlines. Quick context: Silverdirect is negotiating the MSA + a regional order form (US entity). They're pushing for lower minimums and Net 45 with monthly invoicing and PO requirement.

As legal, can you: 1) confirm whether Redwood can accept Net 45 vs our standard Net 30 for hosted accounts (we can make an exception with credit checks / prepay / covenant)? 2) provide a short redline that keeps Redwood's tax allocation language but adds explicit reverse-charge fallback for EU VAT if needed; 3) advise on PO-on-each-invoice requirement (our invoices are generated automatically from the billing system — adding PO is doable but ops needs to know where to put it).

I think we should propose a compromise on minimums: $175k phased over two quarters rather than $150k outright. Grace — can you confirm the commercial impact (unit rates / uplift if we accept lower commit)? I'll loop Finance if we need to allocate early credits.

Thanks Ben — quick read-through and proposed approach below. I attached a redline with tracked changes for the MSA/order form but pulled out the commercial/legal tradeoffs here so we can be aligned before sharing with the customer.

1) Minimum committed spend
- Customer asks for $150k. Operationally we can accept a reduction provided: (a) we adjust the ramp so 50% is due in Q1 and remaining 50% in Q2 (phased commit), or (b) include a make-good clause where unused committed units convert to discounted overage credits.
- Commercial ask: suggest $175k phased (25% upfront credit, remainder split across two monthly invoices in Q1) as Ben suggested — preserves unit economics and gives Silverdirect lower upfront burden.

2) Net terms / invoicing
- Standard Redwood Net 30. Legal can approve Net 45 only with: credit approval from Finance, and a signed PO that references the order form and Redwood's tax/legal name. For a first-year Net 45 concession, include an explicit clause to revert to Net 30 after 12 months unless otherwise agreed.
- Monthly invoicing in arrears is fine; confirm Redwood ops will send invoices on the 1st of each month for prior-month usage. We should add an "invoice dispute" timing clause (e.g., disputes must be raised within 30 days).

3) PO requirement and PO field on invoices
- Acceptable. Ops can include a PO-number field. Important: contract should say "Customer will provide PO for each invoice where required by Customer's internal policy" and Redwood will include the PO on the invoice; do not condition payment obligation on purchase order issuance.

4) VAT / tax allocation
- Proposed language: Customer is responsible for any VAT/GST, and where local law requires Redwood to collect VAT, Redwood will charge VAT on the invoice. Where Customer is eligible for reverse-charge, Customer will self-assess and provide the necessary tax registration evidence. Add a short doc-evidence checklist for EU customers (VAT number, local fiscal docs).

5) Document change and sign flow
- I'll attach redlines to the order form (see Redlines_proposed_by_legal_20261102.docx). Once we agree the minimums + Net terms, we should prepare a DocuSign order form and capture PO number and W-9 (if customer requests tax docs for US payments).

Next steps proposed: Grace to propose the commercial compromise to Evan (prefer $175k phased). I can prepare the tracked-orderform redline for sign-off. Ben — if you want me to soften any clause language, tell me specifically which paragraph to edit.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Evan — thanks for sending the procurement redlines and the PO template. Appreciate the clarity on your AP process.

We reviewed internally with Legal and Finance. To keep the project timeline achievable and protect both sides, here's a pragmatic compromise we can sign off on quickly:

- Minimum committed spend: Redwood can accept a $175,000 minimum (down from our original $200k). To reduce Silverdirect's near-term cash burden, we will phase the minimum across Q1/Q2 2027: 25% as an upfront credit applied to the first invoice, then equal monthly allocations across the first four months after go-live. If after month four the cumulative usage is below the committed amount, the remaining balance will be billed as a final settlement invoice.

- Invoicing cadence & PO: We will invoice monthly in arrears (invoices generated on the 1st for prior month). Redwood will include the customer's PO number on each invoice. Please note that a PO is a reference for our ops team — payment obligations remain per the order form regardless of PO issuance timing.

- Payment terms: We can provide Net 45 for year one subject to (a) a signed PO referencing the order form, and (b) completion of standard credit checks. If credit checks are not completed within 10 business days of signature, Net 30 will apply. After the first 12 months the parties will revert to Net 30 unless both sides agree in writing otherwise.

- VAT / tax: Silverdirect will be responsible for VAT. Redwood will charge VAT where required by law; where Silverdirect's legal entity qualifies for reverse-charge, please provide VAT registration evidence and we will issue an invoice without VAT and include the reverse-charge notation. Legal has prepared suggested contract language to reflect this.

- Next steps: Kimberly has attached a redline with the specific MSA/order-form edits (Redlines_proposed_by_legal_20261102.docx). If Silverdirect is comfortable, we'll load the updated order form into DocuSign and I will send the PowerForm link for signature. Once signature + PO are in place we'll kick off entitlement setup with Finance and Customer Success.

Evan — can you confirm by EOD Friday whether Silverdirect accepts the $175k phased proposal and the Net 45 conditional concession? If yes, we'll push the DocuSign link and target signature next week.

Thanks — Grace
